title: tier-2 shipped code: encoding header parse against the client's EncodingHeaderParse

unreachableBranches.why: The client's `data == NULL` guard jumps to the shared reject block. A harness pointer argument always names a buffer the oracle places in its arena, so RDX is never null and this edge cannot execute from any representable input. The site runs on every call through the non-null fall-through, which is the only edge ever observed; the length-0 case reaches the same reject block through the length gate, so the reject behaviour is still compared.

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/encoding.rs, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the encoding_header_parse entry. The ledger binds the verdict to encoding.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is EncodingHeaderParse at exe 0x142498920. Signature: (void *out, const uint8 *data, uint32 len), returning 0 for an accepted header and 8 for a rejected one in EAX/RAX. The client writes only the low byte of RAX; every value-producing instruction before either return is a MOVZX from a byte or XOR AL, AL, so RAX is exactly 0 or 8 (the emulator starts RAX at zero). The probe returns the same u64.

Output layout, verified against the function bytes: out[0x11]=data[3] (ckey width), out[0x12]=data[4] (ekey width), out[0x18]=be16(data[5..7])<<10 (ckey->ekey page bytes), out[0x20]=be16(data[7..9])<<10 (ekey->espec page bytes), out[0x14]=be32(data[9..13]), out[0x1c]=be32(data[13..17]), out[0x24]=be32(data[18..22]). The client shifts each big-endian field together in that order; write_header_fields follows the same sequence and stores host-order dwords.

Accept gates, in the client's order: data non-null, len >= 22, data[0]=='E', data[1]=='N', data[2]==1, data[17]==0. Only then are the seven fields written. The value checks run after those writes: ckey width 1..16, ekey width 1..16 via (u8)(ekey-1) <= 15, both be16 page sizes non-zero, both be32 page counts non-zero, and the be32 espec block non-zero. A value failure therefore leaves every field written and returns 8 - the fixture compares those bytes too.

The fixture's first case is the install's real 22-byte encoding header: 45 4e 01 10 10 00 04 00 04 00 00 3e 99 00 00 29 17 00 00 16 a6 db. It decodes to version 1, 16/16 keys, 4 KiB pages, 16025 and 10519 pages, byte 17 zero and a 1,484,507-byte espec block, and the shipped EncodingFile::parse opens the real 111,058,223-byte manifest with it.

The out buffer starts at 0xA5 and the data buffer beyond the header at 0x5A, so the memory channel compares every byte the client leaves alone as well as the fields it writes. Both buffers are returned by the probe, so an accidental write to the input header is caught too. The fixture pins every length 0..22 and two longer lengths, all six gate values, ckey/ekey widths 0/1/16/17, each page size and page count at 0/1/0xffffffff, the espec block at 0/1/0xffffffff, and mixed headers.

Coverage: the sweep finds 14 conditional branch sites. 13 reach both edges on the compared runs; the null-data guard's jump edge cannot execute because a pointer argument is never null, so it is declared under unreachableBranches and the harness validates the declaration (site ran, exactly one edge observed, declared edge never observed) before excluding it. Coverage is 100% of the 13 reachable sites.

Mutation: 39 scored mutants, all in write_header_fields. Every gate flip, every shift-count boundary on the two page-size and three count arms, and all eight value-check flips are generated by line order and killed by the pinned corpus, whose first 48 cases include the valid header, every zero edge and every all-ones field.

Not tested: a null data pointer. The harness has no way to pass one (the oracle writes the pointee into its arena and sets RDX to that address), and a null pointer with a large len is a fault in the client too. Length 0 exercises the same reject block and the same 'writes nothing' channel. The 16-byte-width limit of EncodingFile::parse is not part of this parser: the unit pins widths 1..16, which the client accepts, and the page reader's rejection is covered by encoding.rs's own tests.

acknowledgedGaps.why: The harness represents a pointer argument as an arena buffer and always passes its address, so a null RDX is not representable. The client's null guard and the len < 22 guard share the same reject block and both write nothing; the unit covers that block through lengths 0..21, and the declared dead edge is validated by the coverage stage.
